_how_it_could_be_lifted: Section 2 is conditioned on « express written permission by us », which makes this a refusal that can be withdrawn rather than a bar. Contacts the maker publishes: info@shanling.com (technical support) and shop@shanling.com (orders). A written yes would settle both the store clause and the robots reservation at once. Shanling belongs on the letter list, and it is the first entry there whose refusal is partly machine-readable.
_how_to_close_it: Ask. Section 2 of the store terms is conditioned on « express written permission by us », so a written yes settles the prose and the robots reservation at once. Contacts the maker publishes: info@shanling.com and shop@shanling.com. Shanling belongs on the letter list - not among the refusals but among the brands whose answer would unlock a live desktop range: the maker announced « Introducing Shanling EH50 - Desktop DAC & HP Amp » on 2026-11-24.
_cleared_to_harvest_on_the_product_host: Cleared 2026-11-25, after one afternoon as « not established ». Remi decided on 2026-11-25 that a Content-Signal of « ai-train=no, use=reference » is this project's permission to READ a page: « C'est reference. » Recorded in DECISIONS.md with its limits. What it permits: quoting a specification sentence in a sourced claim, with its URL and date - the use the signal names. What it does not touch: a prose clause forbidding reproduction. The 22 brands in the register of refusals stay refused, because a permissive robots.txt does not lift a sentence a lawyer wrote. Shanling's product hosts, shanling.com and en.shanling.com, publish NO page of conditions - every href on the homepage was searched for term, legal, copyright, privacy, policy, disclaimer and condition, with zero matches. What en.shanling.com publishes instead is robots.txt, whose general group is « User-agent: * / Allow: / » with « Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference », plus a sitewide « Disallow: / » for ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai and Claude-Web under a « # Training crawlers » heading - and Claude-User is not among them. So the maker refuses training and permits reference, which is what this catalogue does. Records may be sourced to en.shanling.com.
_NOTHING_may_be_taken_from_the_store: store.shanling.com is a DIFFERENT matter and remains off limits. Its terms forbid reuse outright - « You agree not to reproduce, duplicate, copy, sell, resell or exploit any portion of the Service [...] without express written permission by us » (Section 2) and « you are prohibited from using the site or its content: [...] (i) to spam, phish, pharm, pretext, spider, crawl, or scrape » (Section 12) - and those terms scope themselves to that host by their own preamble: « This website/application is operated by https://store.shanling.com/ team. Throughout the website/application, the terms "we", "us" and "our" refer to https://store.shanling.com/ team. » No record may cite a store URL, and no price, photograph or description from it may be used. The decision on use=reference does not reach a prose clause, and this is the clearest example of why the two must be read separately: one brand, two hosts, two opposite answers.
_the_product_pages_are_images_but_the_SI: All 66 DAC-relevant product pages on en.shanling.com were downloaded and measured on 2026-11-25: every current one is a stack of 12 to 38 sliced JPEGs with zero or one line of real text. EM7's page is 29 images named EM7英文官网_01.jpg to _29.jpg and nothing else; several pages' only text line is « Shop at Amazon.com ». No figure was read off any image. BUT - and this is what separates Shanling from HiFi ROSE and iBasso - the same maker publishes real text in two other places on the same host: its news announcements at /article/NNNNNN, most of which carry a genuine specification list, and its MANUAL PDFs at /catlog/*.pdf and /download/files/*.pdf. The manuals are where the digital-filter menus and the native-DSD statements live, and they appear nowhere else. Four very old product pages do carry on-page text: M0, M1, M2s and M3s. So an image wall is not always a dead end: it can be a wall around one door.
_pdftotext_layout_eats_the_letter_t: A measured extraction trap, worth recording for anyone reading these manuals again. With the fonts Shanling embeds, « pdftotext -layout » SILENTLY DROPS the letter t: « Connec he power adapter ». Default mode (no -layout) extracts cleanly. Every quote taken from a Shanling PDF came from the clean extraction. The failure is silent and plausible-looking, which is the dangerous kind - « 768kHz » survives, but a filter named « Short Delay Sharp » would come back as « Shor Delay Sharp » and be quoted as a maker's typo.
_DoP_appears_NOWHERE_and_native_only_in_: Not one Shanling page or manual uses the term DoP. The word « native » appears in exactly two places: the UA dongle manuals, which all say « Native DSD support up to DSDnnn » in those words, and the EM5 article's « DSD256 native, DSD512 software ». For every other model, whether DSD arrives native or framed in PCM is simply not stated - so `native_dsd` is written on the UA records and on the EM5, and `dop` on none of them. Contrast xDuoo, where « native » was boilerplate repeated on twenty pages and had to be refused: here it appears on a minority of pages, in a consistent sentence, which is what makes it usable.
_the_NOS_question_answered_MODEL_BY_MODE: Shanling sells valve-output devices AND non-oversampling devices, so vocabulary/nos-means-two-things.json applies here more sharply than anywhere. It was resolved per model from the manuals' own menu tables, not from the three letters. NON-OVERSAMPLING, as a named menu or switch item: EC Zero T (« PCM Filter » / « OS/NOS »), EC Play (« PCM Filter: 0-4 » ending in NOS), EH2 (a REAR-PANEL SWITCH, « [FILTER] switch on the rear of the device switches between OS (Oversampling) and NOS (NonOversampling) modes »), EH90 (« Tone Filter »), UA6 II (five filters ending in NOS). VALVES AND NO NOS AT ALL: the UA7, which has « Dual JAN6418 Tubes », a « TUBE / Off/On » menu item, and eight named ESS filters among which there is no NOS entry. The EC Zero T is the hard case - it has BOTH valves and a NOS mode - and only the manual's menu table separates them: « PCM Filter | OS/NOS » is one item and « Tube Mode | Off/On » is another.
_download_pages_that_serve_another_model: Three measured defects in the maker's own download index, each of which would silently attribute one model's figures to another. EC Zero T MAX's download page serves the EC Zero T file. M7T Master's serves the M7T file. And the page labelled M0 Pro serves the M0 PURA manual - byte-identical to the M0 Pura download, its text containing « M0 Pura » seven times and « M0 Pro » zero times. Nothing was attributed across those links.
_what_has_no_text_anywhere: Read and not recorded, because the maker publishes no figure of any kind in text: UA Mini (image-only page, no article, no entry in the download index at all), UA1 (no article and no manual), EC Smart (no product page, and its manual link /catlog/EC-Smart-V1.1.pdf.pdf 404s on a doubled extension), H0 (no product page, and its manual names no part and no rate), M0 Pura, M1s, M6 (21), Q2, M8T, M8T Cu, M7T, M7T Master, UA7 Cu, M9 Plus, and the older M6, M6 PRO, M6 Pro (21), M3X, M8, M2X, Q1 and M5s. Several of their articles point the reader at « full specifications on its product page » - which is the image wall. EH50, by contrast, has NO product page and the best per-input page on the whole site.
